A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from ADSQE to DCSQE. All 13 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original supervised and unsupervised QE results, component ablations, generator/annotator experiments, and appendix analyses of timing, convergence and data scale.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds a self-annotation case study, a manual audit of synthetic examples, and error-category evaluation results.

M1.justification: ADSQE is renamed DCSQE, but the CBS generation, TER alignment, separate Annotator, SPCE aggregation, QE architecture, losses and inference rules remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is identical; the expanded SPCE explanation does not introduce new steps.

E1.justification: Appendix H adds evaluation on a WMT2024 training set described as unseen during model training, using its error-category annotations. The original WMT2022/2023 coverage remains, and no additional language pair is specified.

E2.justification: New Table 13 introduces a model without synthetic-data pretraining as the comparison control. Main benchmark comparator membership is unchanged: COMET becomes CometKiwi, referring to the same cited work and released checkpoint.

E3.justification: Appendix H introduces a random 100-instance manual audit and per-category error-detection accuracy evaluation with and without synthetic pretraining. Appendix G newly reports WMT2022-based threshold calibration, conflicting with the retained WMT2023 calibration description in A.7; the actual calibration procedure cannot be resolved.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused self-annotation case study in Table 10 and Appendix H's manual label audit and error-category analysis. The earlier component ablations, generator/annotator studies, convergence analysis and data-scale analysis remain. Appendix G discusses existing Table 2 results without adding a threshold sweep.

E5.justification: Both versions specify the Williams significance test with p < 0.05 and bold significant results. v3 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or new statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 and the existing ablation and timing tables retain their numerical results, while several Figure 3 points change. New findings include no undetected errors in the 100-example audit and Table 13's category results, such as mistranslation detection accuracy of 43.50% without versus 59.23% with synthetic pretraining.

T1.justification: The mathematical task definitions, scoring and severity equations, and SPCE pseudocode are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs, and v3 adds no formal assumptions, derivations or theorems.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about mitigating distribution shift, using separate generation and annotation models, producing phrase-level labels, and achieving strong supervised and unsupervised QE performance. The framework and comparator renaming does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Appendices B, G and H add arguments about dependency-parsing resource availability, threshold transfer across datasets, and coverage of diverse error types. Appendix C adds detailed interpretations of token labels and severities. The dedicated limitations and main mechanism explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 replaces v1's future code/data-release promise with a specific code URL, clarifies CometKiwi model sizes, and documents nearest-error-rate sampling without replacement for the existing generator analysis. A.4 changes the reported GEMBA identifier from gpt-4-turbo-preview to gpt-4-0125-preview; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zouhar et al. (2024) to connect CometKiwi limitations with distribution shift, and Nivre et al. (2020) and Glavaš and Vulić (2021) to discuss dependency-parsing resources. The broader positioning against earlier QE and synthetic-data methods remains intact.

P1.justification: Changes include consistent DCSQE and CometKiwi terminology, expanded SPCE examples, a rewritten downsampling explanation, fuller case-study discussion, new appendix subsections and acknowledgments. The main section order and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 3 changes from two overlaid plots to six separate panels with revised axes and labels. v3 adds the self-annotation and error-category tables, updates several headers and captions, and relocates retained appendix displays. The overall two-column design and most figures and tables remain.

improvement.justification: The clearer SPCE and downsampling explanations, explicit code link, and added label/error-category checks provide a limited improvement in reproducibility and evidential support. These gains are tempered by unexplained numerical changes in Figure 3 and the conflicting threshold-calibration sources in Appendices G and A.7. The core method and main benchmark results remain unchanged.
